title: Mars near and far
caption: Mars over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A calm night settles over ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile's Atacama Desert. The eye goes first to a bright reddish point left of centre in the sky: the planet Mars. On the hill to the right, ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT) stands in silhouette against the stars.
Along the hilltop you can pick out the domes of the VLT's four 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes and, at the right edge, the smaller VLT Survey Telescope.

In a sense, Mars appears in this picture twice. The desert around Paranal looks uncannily like the Martian surface, and the European Space Agency occasionally brings prototype rovers here to rehearse missions in realistic conditions. The red planet overhead and its earthly stand-in below make a neat pairing, which is what the picture's title, Mars near and far, plays on.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by Farid Char; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Mars would look like a bright reddish point to the eye as well; the camera may also record many fainter stars than an observer would notice.
